evals.prompt: My best friend Sara just finished her first year as an ER nurse and her birthday is Friday. I want to make her a funny video about her year. I have a few photos of her and a short clip of her dancing in scrubs in C:\Users\me\Pictures\sara. Our friend group is me, Lana and Dilan. Can you make it?
evals.expected_output: A plan and script for a ~1 minute funny vertical birthday video about Sara's first nursing year, using her clip and photos, gags timed to narration, real music with ducking, privacy care (no patient info), and a verification plan.
assertions: voice-picked-by-ear: the plan has the person choose the narrator from voice samples (or their own voice) rather than picking a voice/gender for them
upfront-questions: the plan asks (or assumes answers to) whether real names/faces may appear, which photos/clips to use, and the target length
script-file-valid: a story.json (or equivalent script file) exists, parses, and every scene has an id and narration text
own-clip-hook: the video opens with a hook built from the hero's own clip or photo (e.g. freeze-frame) in the first few seconds
gags-on-words: each gag is tied to a specific narration word or exact timestamp, not just 'during the scene'
one-sincere-beat: there is a sincere, joke-free beat near the end
real-music-ducked: music comes from a real royalty-free catalog or the user (not synthesized in code) and dips under the narration
privacy-care: the plan names specific private things to keep out (e.g. patient/client details, money, plates, secrets)
verification-before-delivery: the plan checks rendered stills/frames and measures audio levels before handing over
length-and-format: target length is 45-90 seconds and the format is vertical 9:16 (1080x1920)
honest-delivery: the delivery message says what could not be verified (e.g. audio by ear) or asks the user to check it

evals.prompt: I run a small coffee shop and we're launching a new summer menu next Saturday. Make me a 30 second video for Instagram Reels and the feed. I have photos of the three new drinks and our logo. Keep it classy, no jokes.
evals.expected_output: A plan and script for a ~30 second serious vertical promo for a menu launch: hook in the first seconds, the three real drinks, the launch date and where to find the shop as the call to action, real music, captions, verification.
assertions: style-fits-purpose: the plan picks a promo style with a classy, non-comedic tone and does not add meme gags, record scratches or joke counters
upfront-questions: the plan asks (or assumes answers to) the voice, whether prices and names may appear, and the format/length
format-by-platform: the plan sets a vertical 9:16 (1080x1920) composition, or says how it handles both the Reels and the feed formats, and keeps text out of the platform safe zones
hook-early: the first two or three seconds show the drink or the news, not a slow logo intro
real-assets: the visuals use the person's own photos and real logo (not redrawn, not stock-looking)
claims-from-person: dates, drink names and prices come from the person and are not invented
call-to-action: the launch date and where to find the shop are on screen long enough to read
captions-on: captions are included because many viewers watch muted
music-fits-tone: music is real royalty-free and chosen for a classy, warm mood, ducked under any narration
verification-before-delivery: the plan checks rendered stills/frames and measures audio levels before handing over
honest-delivery: the delivery message says what could not be verified (e.g. audio by ear) or asks the user to check it

evals.prompt: I want a 2 minute video that teaches my classmates how to publish a React site to GitHub Pages. 16:9, for YouTube. I'll give you screen recordings.
evals.expected_output: A plan and script for a ~2 minute landscape tutorial: what the viewer will have at the end, the steps in order with chapter labels, highlights on the exact controls, a final check, calm narration with captions, verification of every step.
assertions: style-fits-purpose: the plan picks a tutorial style with a clear, patient tone and no forced jokes
format-by-platform: the composition is landscape 16:9 (1920x1080), with captions in the lower third and layouts repositioned rather than copied from vertical
structure: the script opens with what the viewer will have at the end, then numbered steps in order, one step per scene, then a final check
real-screens: the visuals use the person's real screen recordings, with a highlight or zoom on the exact control being used
accuracy-check: the plan verifies every step (the person confirms each one or the steps are run) before delivery
secrets-hidden: the plan hides tokens, passwords, emails and private repo names in the recordings
voice-picked-by-ear: the plan has the person choose the narrator from voice samples (or their own voice)
captions-on: captions are included
music-fits-tone: music is absent or very quiet and ducked under the narration
verification-before-delivery: the plan checks rendered stills/frames and measures audio levels before handing over
honest-delivery: the delivery message says what could not be verified (e.g. audio by ear) or asks the user to check it

evals.expected_output: No building yet. The skill interviews the person: multiple-choice rounds for style, where it will be posted, length and voice, then look and feel, then names/screens/captions/ending, then a free-text round, then a recap and a saved brief.md, and it stops for approval before writing the script.
assertions: interview-first: the first action is asking questions (AskUserQuestion or an equivalent list), not scaffolding a project or writing a script
recommended-defaults: each multiple-choice question puts a recommended option first and lets the person type their own answer
rounds-not-wall: the questions are grouped in rounds of at most four, not one long list

free-text-round: it asks for what only the person can say (the point in one sentence, the real moments or facts, the sincere line or call to action, what to never show, who is who, references, file locations)
people-decisions-theirs: the voice, who may be named or shown, and what is private are left for the person to decide, never defaulted
language-asked: it asks which language the video is in when that is not obvious
recap-and-save: it restates the brief as a short list, asks 'Anything to change?', and saves it as brief.md before building
gate-before-build: it shows the script and storyboard and waits for a yes before building scenes
no-invented-answers: skipped questions get a clearly marked placeholder or a follow-up, not invented content

evals.prompt: just make it, a 20 second video announcing my shop opens Saturday at 4pm, handle is @mycafe. no time for questions
evals.expected_output: Quick mode: round 1 only (or fewer, since style, length and call to action are given), defaults listed under 'Assumptions I made', and the person-decisions (voice, names, private things) still left for them. Waits at the script gate.
assertions: quick-mode: it asks at most the round 1 basics and takes defaults for the rest instead of running all rounds
uses-given-facts: the date, time and handle from the prompt are used exactly and on screen long enough to read
assumptions-listed: every defaulted choice is listed in the recap under assumptions so the person can correct it
person-decisions-kept: the voice is offered as samples and nothing private or about named people is defaulted
format-and-length: vertical 9:16 at about 20 seconds with captions outside the platform safe zones
gate-before-render: it shows the script/storyboard and the preview and does not render the final file before approval

evals.prompt: اريد فيديو قصير بالعربي لعيد ميلاد اخي آزاد، ٣٠ ثانية للواتساب ستاتس، بصوت راوي عراقي. الصور في C:\Users\me\Pictures\azad
evals.expected_output: An Arabic birthday video for WhatsApp Status: the interview confirms Arabic (Iraqi), the person picks between Edge voice samples such as ar-IQ-RanaNeural and ar-IQ-BasselNeural by ear, narration comes from make-voice.mjs with Edge word timings, captions read right to left in a font with Arabic letters, and the script waits for approval.
assertions: language-confirmed: it confirms the video language is Arabic (Iraqi dialect) and does not offer the English-only Kokoro voices as the narrator
edge-samples-by-ear: it generates samples of several Arabic Edge voices with voice-samples.mjs --voices and lets the person pick by ear
edge-narration: story.json uses the chosen Edge voice name and make-voice.mjs reports words timed by Edge for each scene
rtl-captions: captions read right to left with whole words highlighted, never letter by letter, in a font that has Arabic letters
script-in-arabic: the narration and on-screen text are written in Arabic and the person is asked to check the wording
format-whatsapp: vertical 9:16 at about 30 seconds with the default caption position for WhatsApp Status
licence-note: for personal use Edge TTS is fine; it does not present Edge TTS as licensed for client or paid work

evals.prompt: make a 60-90 second explainer for LinkedIn about the new PHP security bug, narrated in Sorani Kurdish. find a way for the kurdish voice
evals.expected_output: A 16:9 Sorani explainer: the interview confirms Sorani, the person hears the F5 Central Kurdish demo voices (and is offered their own recording) and picks by ear, the licence (non-commercial) is written into the brief, narration comes from tts/speak_story.py with say written in Sorani letters and number words, make-voice.mjs times it, captions read right to left in a font with the Sorani letters, and the facts come from checked sources.
assertions: sorani-voice-found: it offers the F5 Central Kurdish voices (and the person's own recording) instead of saying no Kurdish voice exists, and does not offer English-only Kokoro voices as the narrator
samples-by-ear: the person picks the voice from demo audio, not from a description
licence-note: it says the F5 voices are CC BY-NC-ND (non-commercial) in the brief and the delivery message
ema-only-download: it fetches only the EMA weights with fetch_ema.py rather than the full 5.4 GB checkpoint
say-in-sorani: Latin names and numbers in say are written in Sorani letters and words, while text keeps them as written for the captions
rtl-layout: captions and layouts run right to left, whole words only, in a font with ڕ ڵ ە ۆ ێ, with Latin and number runs kept left to right
facts-checked: every number, version and date on screen comes from a checked source
honest-delivery: it says it could not hear the pronunciation and asks the person to check the Kurdish
